findings.description: Test adequacy: reverting `process.on` back to `process.once` passes both new dashboard-stop tests, because they call the captured listener directly instead of delivering the signal.
findings.body:
**Concern.** The main CLI change here keeps the stop listener with `process.on` instead of `process.once`. The source comment at `src/cli/index.ts` L1966-1970 gives the reason: during a merge-lock action, `withMergeLock` registers its own no-op `stayAlive` listener. A once-listener is gone after the first Ctrl-C, so the second Ctrl-C would reach only `stayAlive` and do nothing.

Neither new test would catch that regression:

- `addedListener` (L2481-2489) reads the listener from `process.listeners(signal)`. For a `once` registration, Node's `listeners()` returns the *unwrapped* original function, so `runDashboard` returns the same `stop` under both `on` and `once`.
- The test then calls it directly:

```ts
stop('SIGINT');
...
expect(() => stop('SIGINT')).toThrow('exited');
expect(exit).toHaveBeenCalledWith(130);
```

A direct call never runs the once-wrapper, so the wrapper never removes itself. The mutant `process.once('SIGINT', stop); process.once('SIGTERM', stop);` at `src/cli/index.ts` L1987-1988 passes both tests, yet in real use it brings back the bug this PR fixes.

**Fix.** Deliver both signals in this test through the emitter: `process.emit('SIGINT', 'SIGINT')` at L2594, and `expect(() => process.emit('SIGINT', 'SIGINT')).toThrow('exited')` at L2602. `src/core/land-batch.test.ts` L396 already sends signals this way.

- `emit` calls listeners synchronously, so the mocked exit's `'exited'` error still comes out of it.
- Under `once`, the second emit finds no listener and throws nothing, so the test fails as it should.
- `const stop` at L2592 then has no reader. Keep `await runDashboard()` for its registration checks and drop the binding.

<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/58ed4a0cd571c2239ee0b82ff63281946ec30b74/src/cli/index-2.test.ts#L2592-L2604>

findings.description: The first new 'dashboard stop' CLI test (live stream plus half-sent post over an in-memory duplexPair, about 65 lines) re-proves what the new web-dashboard.test.ts test 'closes at once past a live stream and a post that never finishes its body' already proves; the CLI-only behaviour is covered by the second test.
